prize_parts.citation: for their analysis of how organised interests shape trade policy and for integrating innovation and growth into the theory of international trade

statement.case_for: Grossman and Helpman made the political determination of policy a formal, testable object inside trade theory. The protection-for-sale framework explains why trade policy departs from efficiency, and it travelled well beyond trade into the study of lobbying and policy formation generally. Their joint work on innovation, growth and trade is a second strand with lasting theoretical influence. Attribution is the cleanest of any shortlisted entry: a long, tightly coupled two-person partnership with central joint papers and books, and no obvious third claimant on the ballot. The core results are about three decades old and have been extended, tested and absorbed into the field's teaching and applied work. Under common criteria of conceptual generality, durable influence, clear credit and maturity, I keep this first. The opening tallies suggest many colleagues share the view, but I do not treat that as evidence of merit. I use a single-part configuration because adding a second achievement would force a one-person part on another ballot, which would cut against that ballot's own attribution.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is empirical. Tests of the protection-for-sale equilibrium are mixed and sensitive to specification, so part of the case rests on the framework's conceptual and organising power rather than on a confirmed quantitative prediction. A second concern is framing. A citation covering both political economy and growth-and-trade could look like two prizes merged into one, and Helpman's separate firm-heterogeneity work (B030) leaves open how the committee would want trade recognised overall. My assessment also rests on general knowledge, and I have not independently verified citation or impact data.

responses.point: Fredriksson ranks B001 first but notes that empirical support for protection-for-sale is mixed, that the committee might prefer to reward trade through the firm-heterogeneity line, and that he has a limited view of how the endogenous-growth work should be weighted.
responses.response: I agree on the mixed empirical record, and I weigh it as a real limit. I would still separate a model's contribution from the fit of one equilibrium specification. The framework made lobbying and tariff formation measurable and generated a large structural and reduced-form testing literature, and that is a durable contribution even where parameter estimates are fragile. On the choice between lines, I do not think the two strands compete. Firm heterogeneity (B030) is a distinct achievement, with Melitz as its central originator, and an award for it would not substitute for the Grossman-Helpman contribution. For the growth-and-trade strand, I would anchor the citation on policy formation and use the innovation-and-growth work as supporting rather than co-equal, which keeps the citation tight.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B001 first, treats Grossman and Helpman as the clear core pair, and flags possible overlap with Krugman's 2008 prize and the complication of Helpman's separate firm-heterogeneity credit.
responses.response: I accept the overlap question but think it is manageable. The 2008 recognition concerned trade patterns and economies of scale. The political-economy-of-protection contribution and the open-economy endogenous-growth contribution address different questions, namely why policy is what it is and how trade and innovation interact. I read Helpman's presence on B030 as a reason to word the citation carefully, not a reason to weaken B001. A two-person B001 prize leaves the firm-heterogeneity question open, and I do not see a need to resolve it in this round.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B018 first, credits it with combining new data, credible designs and a framework, and sees a real attribution problem at three names (Autor, Hanson, Katz, with Dorn and task-model antecedents also in play).
responses.response: I rank B018 second myself and see the strength Hjalmarsson describes: credible designs with conceptual framing and large policy influence. Our difference is mainly about attribution and maturity. The China-shock work is Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The task framework has antecedents outside the credited names. Katz's skill-premium contributions are a third strand. The cap of three therefore forces a cut that I find harder to defend than the two-person B001 attribution. The trade-shock findings are also still being qualified on persistence and identification, which is a healthy sign but argues for a little more time. I keep B018 as my first alternative rather than my preferred part, and I would revisit if colleagues can show a defensible three-name core.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B001 first, notes that the Helpman-Grossman credit is concentrated but that the citation must be drawn carefully between trade policy and innovation-driven growth, and raises possible overlap with the 2025 growth prize.
responses.response: I agree that the framing question is the most useful open issue in the B001 case. My proposed citation leads with organised interests and trade policy, because that is where the contribution is most distinctive, and it names innovation and growth as an integration into trade theory. On the 2025 overlap, I rely on colleagues' description of that prize as covering innovation-led growth. The Grossman-Helpman growth-and-trade work is about the open economy and about how trade affects innovation incentives, which is a different object, though I would want the committee to confirm this and I have not verified the details of that prize.

uncertainties: How much weight the mixed empirical record of protection-for-sale should carry against its conceptual and organising influence.

Whether the citation should lead with trade policy and political economy or give equal billing to innovation-driven growth, and whether the committee sees overlap with the 2008 trade prize or the 2025 growth prize.
Whether B018 would become preferable if the committee can agree a defensible three-name core among Autor, Dorn, Hanson and Katz.
My assessments rest on general knowledge and colleagues' stated facts, without independent verification of citation or impact data.
statement.conflict_note: No profile-based connection to the credited names on B001 is apparent; Grossman and Helpman are trade economists and my profile lists no collaboration with them. For the alternative B036, my profile lists a co-authored corruption paper with Torsten Persson and Bo Rothstein (Governance), and my opening noted a Stockholm University connection to Persson. That would be a possible recusal consideration if B036 were pursued, and I disclose it without adjudicating it. I also work on democratisation, measurement of democracy and quality of government, which is close to B036's subject, and I have tried to apply the same criteria as for other fields.
